podcasts.title: Why Real-World AI Is Harder Than the Benchmark | EliseAI’s Mario Martone
podcasts.summary: What changes when an AI mistake doesn’t just hurt a benchmark score, but affects someone’s housing or healthcare? EliseAI Head of Applied Research Mario Martone argues that deploying AI in essential industries requires a very different standard of reliability. Mario joins MTS to explain how EliseAI handles roughly 5 million phone calls a month, why LLMs aren’t the right solution for every problem, and how the team combines language models, traditional machine learning, neural networks, and internally built evaluations to decide what actually works in production. Drawing on 15 years studying theoretical physics, Mario also explains how the scientific method shapes EliseAI’s research culture, from testing new models against its own benchmarks to fine-tuning open-source models and automating increasingly complex workflows across housing and healthcare. And he makes the case that applying AI to the real world can produce problems every bit as intellectually difficult as the ones he encountered studying string theory. podcasts.title: Sparse attention fixes memory bandwidth, not memory capacity.
podcasts.summary: Sparse attention fixes memory bandwidth, not memory capacity. “The whole idea of HiCache is trying to offload KV cache from the HBM to a lower tier, higher capacity but lower bandwidth memory, and only load the most relevant set of tokens during computation.” “Sparse attention doesn’t mitigate the memory capacity bottleneck. It’s a technique that helps a lot with memory bandwidth.” “During the sparse attention computation, you still need to select the tokens. So you still have to keep all the tokens in context, and you cannot discard them. At some point, it still has to be loaded into HBM.” “That’s where HiSparse becomes useful, because it can apply the typical caching rules so that you could load the most relevant parts into HBM.” Watch Full Podcast on YouTube.

podcasts.title: Can Open Models Keep Up With the AI Frontier? | Nathan Lambert
podcasts.summary: a16z Partner Lisha Li sits down with AI researcher and Trillium founder Nathan Lambert to ask how durable the gap really is between frontier AI labs and open models. Nathan argues that OpenAI and Anthropic have structural advantages in compute, capital, and the ability to pioneer new training paradigms, but open-model labs, particularly in China, have proven remarkably capable of following close behind. They unpack how much of that comes from distillation versus technical talent, why compute remains a major constraint, and how data, RL environments, and post-training are increasingly shaping model progress. They also discuss Nathan’s new nonprofit research lab, Trillium, and its plans to open up parts of AI research that are increasingly difficult to study from the outside. That includes releasing RL environments and documenting how AI is actually being used to automate AI research, with the goal of demystifying recursive self-improvement and giving researchers and policymakers a clearer picture of what frontier systems can and cannot do. podcasts.summary: Our next guest on the Senior Decision Makers series is Erlina Yeo Terwelp, a Managing Director at Columbia Investment Management Company, where she oversees the endowment's private markets portfolio. Erlina's path spans investment banking, private equity, growth equity, and family office investing before she joined Columbia nearly a decade ago. Our conversation covers her evolution as an allocator, how she thinks about manager selection and portfolio construction, the growing role of leadership and team development in her seat, and her perspective on generalist versus specialist team models after working within both. Erlina is candid, thoughtful, and funny — with a deep commitment to intellectual honesty, an openness to changing her mind, and a willingness to continually put herself in situations that force her to grow.
